bio: Tucked away behind an unshowy entrance, this restaurant is located between City Hall and the old port, next to the Château Ramezay. Part of its appeal lies in the historical character of the setting with its thick stone walls and wooden beams. With subdued lighting and cozy leather armchairs, the atmosphere is intimate and romantic, reminiscent of an upscale club. The menu changes regularly to reflect the seasons and showcases local ingredients. Dishes include vol-au-vent with veal sweetbreads and lobster, halibut in a white wine sauce with bacon jam, trout gently confit in olive oil, and American Wagyu beef with pommes dauphines and Choron sauce.
